activity: playing on a sports team for the season
knowledge_domain: playing on a sports team for the season
fact: Players drink water during breaks, especially on hot days.
story:
Benjamin was playing soccer in his backyard. His team wore red shirts. The sun was hot up in the sky. A butterfly flew by the goal.

Benjamin ran and kicked the ball. He ran some more. His legs felt slow. His mouth felt dry. "I need a drink," he said.

But his water bottle was inside the house. Benjamin sat down on the grass. He watched a ladybug crawl on his shoe. Then Daddy came out with a big cup. "Here is some cold water," Daddy said. Benjamin drank it all up. It was juicy cold and good.

Then he ran back to the game. He kicked the ball into the goal. "Hooray!" said his team. Daddy held up the cup and smiled.

activity: basic shape concepts such as circle, square, triangle and rectangle
knowledge_domain: basic shape concepts such as circle, square, triangle and rectangle
fact: Cutting a square from one corner to the opposite corner makes two triangles.
story:
Wyatt sat at the art table. He wanted to make a paper sailboat. The boat needed two triangles for sails. He looked in the paper tray. He found only one square. No triangles at all. Wyatt felt upset.

"I need triangles," he said.

Miss Ana came over. "Bring your square," she said. "Let's ask Mr. Cole to help." Mr. Cole used the scissors. He cut from one corner to the opposite corner. The square fell apart. Two triangles! Wyatt clapped his hands.

"Again!" he said. Mr. Cole gave him another square. Mr. Cole cut it the same way. Two more triangles!

Wyatt taped two triangles on his boat. He taped a circle for the sun. He drew a square house. He planted a little paper flag on top.

Miss Ana held up his boat. "Look at that," she said.

"My boat can sail to the cat," Wyatt said. The class cat was sleeping by the door. It opened one eye and yawned.

activity: pretend play scenarios such as playing house, caring for toys and role-playing simple situations
knowledge_domain: pretend play scenarios such as playing house, caring for toys and role-playing simple situations
fact: Dress-up clothes help you pretend to be someone else.
story:
Hazel loved the dress-up corner at school. There was a box of hats and coats and shiny shoes. But today Ben grabbed the big red hat first. Hazel wanted that hat so much. "My turn soon?" she asked. "Soon," said Ben.

Ben put on the big red hat. He stood up very tall. "I am a firefighter!" he yelled, in a happy way. He picked up a toy baby and rocked it slow and gentle. "The baby is safe now," he said. Hazel watched. The hat had made Ben into someone new. It was like magic.

Soon it was Hazel's turn. She put the big red hat on her head. It slid down over her eyes. She pushed it back up. Now she was a firefighter too! She marched to the toy kitchen. She found the toy dog in the middle of the floor. "Don't worry, little dog," she said. She tucked the dog under a soft blanket. Then she stirred a pretend pot of soup.

Ben sat down next to her. "Firefighters eat soup too," he said. "Yes," said Hazel. "The best soup in town." She held out the wooden spoon to him. "Want a taste?"

activity: hosting a grandparent who comes to stay for a week
knowledge_domain: hosting a grandparent who comes to stay for a week
fact: A grandparent can tell stories about when a child's mom or dad was little.
story:
Grandma came on the big blue bus. She let Ali carry her small red bag. "You can be my helper," she said. Ali puffed up his chest. He was a very good helper.

In the kitchen, Dad made pancakes. Ali sat on his stool and watched. Grandma sat next to him. "Dad," said Ali, "were you ever little?" Dad laughed. "Yes, silly. Long ago." Ali shook his head. "No. Dads are big. Like a bus."

Grandma leaned close. "I will tell you a secret," she said. "Your dad was little like you. He had a small bike. It was green." Ali's eyes went wide. "Dad had a bike?" "And he fell in a puddle," said Grandma. "Splash! Mud on his nose." Ali laughed so hard his stool wobbled.

After breakfast, Ali ran to the garage. He found Dad's old bike bell. Ding, ding! "Dad, you rang this when you were little?" Dad's face turned pink. "Yes. And Grandma has more stories." Ali clapped his hands. "Every day you are here, tell one!" Grandma smiled. "Deal. Tomorrow, the tale of the runaway hat." Ali hugged the bell tight. Ding, ding, ding!

activity: playing on a sports team for the season
knowledge_domain: playing on a sports team for the season
fact: Teams warm up by running or stretching before a game.
story:
Clara put on her red team hat. Her shoes had little white laces. The baseball diamond was bright and green. The dirt smelled like warm dust.

"Play now!" said Clara. She ran to home plate. Coach Mia shook her head and smiled. "First we warm up," she said. "Everyone runs to the fence and back." Clara wanted to swing the bat. But she got in the line anyway.

The team ran to the fence. Clara's feet went pat, pat, pat on the dirt. Then they stretched. Clara touched her toes. She reached up high like a tall tree. Her arms felt loose and good.

Then the game began. Clara ran to first base. Her legs felt fast and springy. She caught a ball with her mitt. Thump! It landed right in the soft pocket.

After the game, Dad gave Clara a piggyback ride to the car. The field was quiet now. "Again tomorrow?" asked Clara. "Yes," said Dad. "First we run, then we play." Clara smiled and hugged her mitt all the way home.

activity: basic emotions such as happy, sad, angry, scared and excited
knowledge_domain: basic emotions such as happy, sad, angry, scared and excited
fact: Taking slow, deep breaths can help your body calm down when you feel angry.
story:
Luka went to the library with his dad. He wanted the big red book about trucks. But a girl named Mia had it first.

Mia held the book tight. Luka grabbed the edge. "It's mine!" he shouted. His face felt hot. His hands made tight fists. He was angry.

Luka stomped to a soft chair. He sat down hard. Dad sat next to him. "Let's try slow breaths," Dad said. Dad breathed in slowly. Luka watched. He breathed in slowly too. Then he let it out, slow and long. They did it again, like a sleepy bear waking up.

Luka's hands went soft. His tummy felt calm. He walked back to Mia. "Can we look at it together?" he asked. Mia smiled a sweet smile. "Yes," she said.

They turned the pages side by side. Luka pointed at a blue truck in the water. "Big wheels!" said Mia. Luka laughed. "Best library day ever," he said.

activity: to count a group of up to ten objects and say which of two groups has more
knowledge_domain: to count a group of up to ten objects and say which of two groups has more
fact: The last number you say when counting tells how many there are altogether.
story:
"Snack time!" called Miss Ana. It was summer, and a stormy sky sat outside the window. Sienna ran to the table.

Two bowls waited there. One bowl had crackers. One bowl had apple slices.

"How many crackers?" asked Miss Ana.

Sienna pointed. "One, two, three, four, five, six, seven." She looked up. "Seven!"

"Yay! And the apples?"

"One, two, three, four, five." Sienna clapped. "Five!"

"Now, which bowl has more?"

Sienna looked at the crackers. She looked at the apples. The cracker bowl looked fuller.

"The crackers!" she cried. "Seven is more than five!"

Miss Ana gave her a cracker from the big bowl. Sienna munched it and grinned.

"More counting after snack," said Miss Ana.

"Yes!" said Sienna. "I love counting!"

activity: learning to swim at the local pool
knowledge_domain: learning to swim at the local pool
fact: A lifeguard's job is to watch the swimmers and help anyone who needs it.
story:
Parker stood by the little backyard pool. The water was warm. His green float looked like a turtle.

Dad got in first. "Kick your legs," said Dad. Parker held the edge. He kicked and kicked. The water made waves. The waves pushed the turtle float. It moved away from him.

"I can't reach it!" said Parker.

Dad pointed. "Look who can help."

Nina the lifeguard sat up in her tall chair. She blew her whistle, one small toot. Then she pointed at the turtle too. From up high, she could see the whole pool. She saw Dad reach out and catch it.

After swimming, Parker sat on the towel for lunch. He watched Nina watch the water.

"Can I chase you to the door?" said Dad.

"Only if you count to ten!" said Parker.

"Ready," said Dad. "One, two, three..."

activity: opposite pairs such as big and small, hot and cold, fast and slow
knowledge_domain: opposite pairs such as big and small, hot and cold, fast and slow
fact: Long and short are opposites.
story:
Emily wanted to dress up like a queen. She found a red scarf in the toy box. She put it on. It dragged on the floor. It went trip, trip, trip behind her feet. "This scarf is too long," said Emily.

Her brother Sam came in. He had a blue scarf. His scarf stopped at his knees. It was short. Emily's scarf was long. "Look," said Sam. "Yours is long. Mine is short." Emily looked and looked. How funny, she thought.

Then Emily had an idea. She wrapped the long scarf around her neck two times. Now it was short! She marched like a queen around the kitchen. Daddy was stirring a big pot on the stove. The pot was hot, so Emily stood back. She waved from far away. Steam went up, up, up. Was it true that steam could swim in the air? It looked like a little cloud dancing. "Our queen is here," said Daddy with a bow.

activity: planting a vegetable garden and watching it grow
knowledge_domain: planting a vegetable garden and watching it grow
fact: A tiny new plant poking up out of the soil is called a sprout.
story:
Milo went to the farmers' market with Dad. They stopped at a seed stand. Milo picked a little bag of carrot seeds. "I want to grow carrots," he said. Dad paid for the seeds.

At home, Milo planted them near the fence. He patted the soil down. Then he waited. Each day he looked at the dirt. No carrots came up. "Maybe they are lost," Milo said. Dad said, "Let's wait a little more."

Milo checked again and again. On a warm morning, he saw something tiny and green. It poked up out of the soil. Milo ran to Dad. "A sprout! There is a sprout!" he shouted. Dad smiled. A bird flew by with twigs for its nest. Milo stood by his sprout and waved. "Grow big, little sprout," said Milo.

activity: searching for a lost favorite toy
knowledge_domain: searching for a lost favorite toy
fact: If you lose something in a busy place, you tell your grown-up instead of going to search by yourself.
story:
Hunter loved his little blue truck. He took it to school for playground time. He pretended the truck could zoom down the slide. Zoom, zoom, it went.

Then it was time for snack. Hunter sat on the bench to eat. After snack, he looked in his pocket. The truck was not there. "Oh no," said Hunter. "Where did my truck go?"

The playground was big. There were kids running everywhere. Hunter wanted to run and look all by himself. But then he saw his teacher, Miss Ana. She was standing by the fence. Hunter walked to her first. "Miss Ana, I lost my blue truck," he said. "Will you help me look?"

Miss Ana smiled. "What a polite thing to do, asking me first. Let's look together." They walked past the slide. They looked under the swing. Then Hunter saw something by the sandbox. It was small and blue. "There it is!" he shouted. His heart felt warm and happy.

Hunter hugged his truck. "Thank you, Miss Ana," he said. She held out her hand. "Let's go line up together," she said. Hunter put the truck safely in his pocket and held her hand all the way.

activity: basic time concepts such as yesterday, today, tomorrow, now and later
knowledge_domain: basic time concepts such as yesterday, today, tomorrow, now and later
fact: Soon means in a little while.
story:
Daniel sat in his car seat. Today they were going to the library. Yesterday he had lost his doll there. Maybe it was still there now.

"Are we there yet?" asked Daniel.
"Not yet," said Mama. "Soon."
Daniel watched out the window. One red car. Two green trees. One big blue bus. "What does soon mean?" he asked.
"Soon means in a little while," said Mama.
So Daniel counted things to pass the time. One cow. Two fences. One yellow house. He pulled his hat down over his ears. The car went around one more corner. Then the library door came into view.

"Here now!" said Daniel. He ran to the desk. The librarian held up his doll. "Found it yesterday," she said. "Storytime starts soon," she added.
Daniel sat on the mat with his doll. He counted to ten. Then the story lady clapped her hands.
"Soon was not very long at all," whispered Daniel to his doll.

activity: to wash their hands with soap for twenty seconds before eating and after the toilet
knowledge_domain: to wash their hands with soap for twenty seconds before eating and after the toilet
fact: After playing outside or petting an animal, it is time to wash your hands.
story:
Felix petted the big brown dog. The dog was soft and a little stinky. Then Felix smelled lunch. Soup! His tummy said yum.

Felix walked to the table. Mama said, "Not yet, Felix. Where are you going?" Felix looked at his hands. They had dog hair on them. He wondered what to do.

"Wash my hands!" said Felix. "Yes," said Mama. "Wash your hands." Felix went to the sink. Mama turned on the water. It was warm but not hot. Felix got the soap. He rubbed and rubbed.

"Sing the song," said Mama. Felix sang the ABC song. He sang it slow. Bubbles covered his hands. One bubble fell to the floor. Pop! Felix kept singing. When the song was done, he rinsed the soap off.

Mama gave him a towel. His hands were clean and warm. Then Mama put the soup on the table. Felix climbed into his chair. He picked up his spoon. "Clean hands, yummy soup," said Felix. "Clean hands, yummy soup," said Mama. Then Felix took a big slurp.

activity: to put on a coat and zip it up by themselves
knowledge_domain: to put on a coat and zip it up by themselves
fact: If your shirt gets caught in the zipper, pulling the zipper back down a little can free it.
story:
Chloe stood in the kitchen by the back door. Snow was falling outside, all wild and white. Mom said, "Time for your coat." Chloe wanted to put it on all by herself.

She pushed her arms in. One arm hid inside the sleeve at first. She shook it and shook it. Out came her hand. Now for the zipper. She pulled it up, up, up. Then it stopped. It was stuck on her red sweater.

Chloe pulled hard. Still stuck. She took a breath. She pulled the zipper back down, just a little. Then she tugged her sweater free. The zipper slid up, up, up to the very top. Chloe smiled at Mom. "I did it," she said. Mom opened the door, and Chloe stepped out into the soft white snow.

activity: the rote number words from one to ten heard in counting songs and everyday counting
knowledge_domain: the rote number words from one to ten heard in counting songs and everyday counting
fact: A number word always means the same amount: 'three' always means three things.
story:
Grandpa lived in a house with a big kitchen. On a rainy day, Alexis put on one red sock and one blue sock. Then he ran to the kitchen.

"Can I have grapes?" he asked.

"Yes," said Grandma. "You can have three grapes."

Alexis looked at the bowl. "The big ones?" he asked. "Or the little ones?"

"Three is three," said Grandma, smiling.

Alexis picked three big grapes. He counted them out loud. "One, two, three." He put them on his plate. He ate them all up.

Then he picked three little grapes. He counted again. "One, two, three." Still three! Big or little, three was three.

"Grandpa wants grapes too," said Alexis.

He counted four grapes this time. "One, two, three, four. Grandpa gets one more than me!"

Grandpa clapped his hands. "Thank you, Alexis. Four grapes for me."

Grandma poured milk into a small cup. Alexis heard the milk go glug, glug. Outside, the rain went tap, tap, tap on the window.

"Let's sing the counting song," said Grandpa.

They sang together. "One, two, three, four, five." Alexis held up his fingers, one by one. "Six, seven, eight, nine, ten!"

"Now wash your hands," said Grandma, "and we will bake bread."

Alexis counted the soap bubbles. "One, two, three, four, five!"

Grandma laughed. "You count everything, Alexis."

"Ten kisses for Grandma!" said Alexis. He gave her one big kiss. "One," he said.

activity: searching for a lost favorite toy
knowledge_domain: searching for a lost favorite toy
fact: The last place you remember having something is a good place to start looking.
story:
Abigail could not find her bunny. Bunny was her favorite toy. She looked under her bed. No bunny there. She looked in her toy box. No bunny there either.

"Where did you see bunny last?" asked Mom. Abigail thought hard. She remembered something. She had bunny at snack time. She ate crackers at the little table. Then she went to play on her slide outside.

Abigail ran to the snack table. She got down on her knees. She peeked under the table. There was bunny! Bunny had fallen down. Bunny was sitting by the chair leg. Abigail grabbed bunny and hugged him tight.

"I found him!" she said. Mom smiled big. "You remembered where you had him," said Mom. "That helped a lot." Abigail nodded. Then she put bunny on the table. She got one cracker for herself. She got one cracker for bunny too.

After snack, Abigail took bunny outside. She held bunny in her lap at the top of the slide. "Ready, bunny?" she said. Down they went, whee, all together.

activity: bringing home a first pet and learning to care for it
knowledge_domain: bringing home a first pet and learning to care for it
fact: Dogs and cats need a bowl of fresh, clean water every day.
story:
Ellie went to the pet store with Dad. She saw a little gray kitten in a cage. "Can we take him home?" she asked. Dad smiled. "Yes, he can be your first pet." They bought a soft bed, a small bowl, and a bag of food.

At home, the kitten drank and drank. Then he went to sleep. Ellie played with her blocks near him. Later she looked at the bowl. It was empty! Not one drop was left.

"Kitty, are you thirsty?" she asked. "I will get you more." She carried the bowl to Dad. "Please fill it up." Dad turned on the tap and filled it with fresh, clean water. Ellie set the bowl down. The kitten ran over and drank it all. "We will fill it every day," Ellie said. "Then you will never be sorry and thirsty." Dad nodded. "Good helper," he said. The kitten licked Ellie's hand and purred like a tiny motor.

activity: to name the primary colours and mix two of them to make a new colour
knowledge_domain: to name the primary colours and mix two of them to make a new colour
fact: Red, yellow and blue are called the primary colours.
story:
Leon had three little paint pots. One pot was red. One pot was yellow. One pot was blue. Red, yellow and blue, that was all.

Leon wanted to paint a rainbow. But a rainbow needs green. Leon looked and looked. No green pot. "Sorry, Leon," said Mama. "That is all the paint we have."

Leon dipped his brush in the yellow paint. He made a yellow sun. Then he dipped the same brush in the blue paint. He made blue water below the sun.

Then something happened. The blue water turned green where it touched the yellow sun. Leon leaned close. Green! Soft, leafy green, like the deep ocean waves in his book.

Leon clapped his hands. He painted a green tree. He painted green grass. "Green, green, green," he said, and laughed.

Mama hung the painting on the fence. Leon stepped back to look. The yellow sun sank down behind his green, green tree. "I made green," Leon said. "All by myself."

activity: going on a family trip away from home
knowledge_domain: going on a family trip away from home
fact: Families pack clothes that fit the weather where they are going, like a swimsuit for the beach or a warm coat for the snow.
story:
Connor opened his brown suitcase on the big hotel bed. "We go to the beach tomorrow!" he said. He pulled out his little swimsuit. It had fish on it.

Then he looked out the window. White snow was falling. Lots of snow. "Oh no," said Connor. "No beach?"

Dad came over and looked out too. "The beach is far away, kiddo. Here it snows. We need warm things." He dug in the suitcase. He found Connor's mittens and his puffy coat.

But the mittens were small. They were for the baby cousin. "Too little!" Connor yelled. He wiggled his fingers. They would not fit.

Mom knelt down beside him. "Let's check the other bag." Connor helped her look. He pulled out a sock. Then a truck. Then, at the bottom, he found his big blue mittens!

He put them on. They fit just right. The next morning, Connor wore his coat and mittens in the snow. He made a snowball and threw it at Dad. "Got you!" said Dad, laughing. "Again!" said Connor.

activity: watching a big game with family and friends
knowledge_domain: watching a big game with family and friends
fact: Each team wears its own colors so you can tell the two teams apart.
story:
Aiden sat on Grandpa's big soft couch. The room smelled like warm popcorn. Everyone was shouting at the TV. "Go, go, go!" they yelled.

Aiden pointed at the screen. "Who has the ball?" he asked. The men all looked the same to him. He counted them. "One, two, three, four. Too many men!"

Grandpa laughed. "Look at the shirts," he said. He held up his mug. "Blue like this, that is one team. Yellow, that is the other team."

Aiden looked hard. The yellow shirt man ran. "Yellow man has the ball!" he said. Grandma clapped. "That's right, Aiden!"

The yellow man kicked the ball far. "Goal!" everyone yelled. Aiden jumped up and down. Uncle Sam gave him a high five. Aiden's finger tapped Uncle Sam's hand. Tap, tap, tap.

Later Aiden painted a picture at the little table. He drew one team in blue. He drew one team in yellow. "Blue team, yellow team," he said. He held the paper up to Grandpa.

"Look, Grandpa! I can tell them apart now."

Grandpa gave him a thumbs up. "Blue team scores!" said Grandpa, and he pointed at the paper with his sharp pencil.

activity: to wash their hands with soap for twenty seconds before eating and after the toilet
knowledge_domain: to wash their hands with soap for twenty seconds before eating and after the toilet
fact: A grown-up should check that the water is warm, not hot, before you wash.
story:
Hayden went to the pharmacy with his dad. His tummy felt funny, so they came for medicine. At the door there was a little sink. A sign said, "Wash your hands."

Hayden wanted to wash his hands all by himself. He turned the tap. Dad put his hand under the water first. "Not yet," said Dad. Hayden waited. Dad turned the tap a little more. "Now it is warm," said Dad. Hayden put his hands in. The water felt like a warm bath.

Then Dad poured soap into Hayden's hands. "Let's count to twenty," said Dad. They counted, "One, two, three, four, five." The soap made white bubbles. The bubbles looked like little clouds. "Ten, eleven, twelve." The water began to rain down on the bubbles. "Nineteen, twenty!" Hayden rinsed all the bubbles away.

A woman in a white coat gave Hayden a sticker. It had a bear on it. "Next time, I will wash my hands too," said Hayden. Dad smiled and held his hand as they walked out.

activity: to clap along to the steady beat of a song and sing a nursery rhyme from memory
knowledge_domain: to clap along to the steady beat of a song and sing a nursery rhyme from memory
fact: Singing a song again and again helps you learn its words by heart.
story:
Eva sat on the red rug at school. Miss Tam put on a song. It had a steady beat, like this: clap, clap, clap.

Eva clapped her hands. First she clapped too fast. Then she clapped too slow. Miss Tam clapped the steady beat. Eva watched. She clapped, clap, clap. Her hands matched the song now.

Then Miss Tam sang a rhyme. "Twinkle, twinkle, little star." Eva knew that line. But the second line slipped away. "How does it go?" she asked.

"Sing it with me," said Miss Tam. So they sang. Then they sang it again. Then again. Eva sang the rhyme many, many times.

After lunch, Eva sat by the blocks. She sang the rhyme all alone. The second line popped out. "How I wonder what you are!" It came by itself, like a huge yawn.

The song played again. Eva clapped the steady beat and sang every word. Miss Tam gave her a thumbs up.

"Again?" said Eva. "Again," said Miss Tam.

activity: basic color words such as red, blue, yellow and green
knowledge_domain: basic color words such as red, blue, yellow and green
fact: Mixing red paint and yellow paint makes orange paint.
story:
Weston ran into Grandma's kitchen. He wanted to paint a pumpkin for the fall table. Grandma had red, blue, yellow and green paint. But there was no orange paint!

"How will I make my pumpkin?" Weston asked. Grandma smiled. "Try mixing two paints," she said. Weston stared at the little cups. It was a puzzle. He picked blue and yellow first. He stirred them with his brush. Green! "That is not orange," he said.

Then he tried red and yellow. He stirred and stirred. Orange! His brush made a big round pumpkin shape. "Grandma, look!" he shouted. Grandma held it up to the window. The painted pumpkin glowed like fire. Weston laughed and painted a green stem on top. "This is my favorite one," he said.

activity: weather words such as sunny, rainy, windy and snowy and the clothes that go with them
knowledge_domain: weather words such as sunny, rainy, windy and snowy and the clothes that go with them
fact: An umbrella keeps rain off your head.
story:
Jackson wanted to play at the park. But the sky was not sunny today. Gray clouds sat over the swings. Big drops began to fall. Rain patted the slide. Rain patted Jackson's head too.

"Come here," said Grandma. She opened her umbrella. It went pop over their heads. Jackson looked up. The rain hit the umbrella. The rain did not hit him. "We share," said Grandma, and they walked under it together.

The wind blew a leaf past them. It spun like a small red top. Jackson picked it up. "This leaf stayed dry under here," he said. Grandma smiled. "You keep it," she said. The rain kept falling on the grass. But Jackson and Grandma stayed dry all the way home. Jackson held the leaf tight.

activity: to hold a pencil correctly and write the letters of their own first name
knowledge_domain: to hold a pencil correctly and write the letters of their own first name
fact: Pressing too hard on a pencil can break its tip.
story:
Wren sat at the big table. She had a pencil and some paper. "I want to write my name," she said. "All by alone." Mama sat next to her. "You can try," said Mama. "I am right here."

Wren held the pencil in her fist. She pressed down hard. She made a big W. Then the pencil tip snapped off. The pencil would not write anymore. "Oh no," said Wren. "It broke!"

"Why did it break?" she asked. "Let's look," said Mama. She gave Wren a new pencil. This time Wren pressed soft and slow. The W came out wiggly but whole. The tip stayed on. Wren made a face of surprise. Then she laughed.

She wrote W, then R, then E, then N. "Wren!" she said. "That is me!" She held up the paper. Mama clapped. Wren wrote her name again, soft and slow, all by herself at the table.

activity: starting the first day of school
knowledge_domain: starting the first day of school
fact: A teacher is the grown-up who looks after and helps the children in a class.
story:
Jasmine stood by the school kitchen door. It was her first day. She held her lunch box tight. The cafeteria was big. Very big. A lady in a yellow apron came out. She carried a tray of tasty apple slices. The lady smiled at Jasmine.

"Are you a teacher?" Jasmine asked in a tiny voice. "Yes, I am Teacher Meg," said the lady. "I look after the children in your class." Teacher Meg held out an apple slice. Jasmine took it. It was sweet and crunchy.

Jasmine felt bigger somehow. She skipped to a table. A boy sat there all alone. "Hello, I am Jasmine," she said, loud and clear. "Want some apple?" The boy grinned and took a bite.

activity: pretend play scenarios such as playing house, caring for toys and role-playing simple situations
knowledge_domain: pretend play scenarios such as playing house, caring for toys and role-playing simple situations
fact: Friends playing pretend together can agree on what happens next.
story:
Arthur ran up to Mia's door. He could not wait to play.

Mia had a big toy dragon on the floor. "Roar!" she said. "The dragon is scary."

Arthur stopped. He wanted the dragon to be nice. "Can the dragon be friendly?" he asked.

Mia thought. Then she smiled. "Yes! The dragon is friendly. He lives in a blue house."

Arthur clapped. Now they both liked the game!

Mia put a blanket on the floor. "This is the dragon's nest," she said. Arthur put the dragon inside. Then he tucked a teddy bear in next to it. "The bear is the dragon's baby," Arthur whispered. Mia giggled.

The baby bear got sleepy. "What will help him sleep?" Mia asked.

"I know!" said Arthur. He patted the bear's back, slow and soft. He hummed a little song. The bear closed his eyes. "Shh," said Mia. "The baby is sleeping."

Then the doorbell rang. Ding dong! It was the pretend mailman. That was Mia's big brother with a box. "Mail for the dragon's house!" he called.

Arthur ran to get it. Inside the box was a paper crown. "A party hat!" he said. "The dragon is having a birthday!"

Mia put the crown on the dragon's head. "Happy birthday, dragon!" they both shouted.

Then Arthur whispered, "Shh, not too loud. The baby is still sleeping."

Mia nodded. They sang the birthday song very, very quietly. The dragon blew out the pretend candles all by himself.

activity: common daily routines such as eating, sleeping, bathing and getting dressed
knowledge_domain: common daily routines such as eating, sleeping, bathing and getting dressed
fact: Pajamas are clothes we wear to sleep in.
story:
Muhammad sat at the dinner table. His plate was full of rice. He took a big bite. He drank his milk. Then he yawned a big yawn.

Muhammad wanted to wear his fire truck shirt to bed. It was his favorite shirt. He wore it at the park. He wore it at school. He asked Dad, "Can I sleep in my fire truck shirt?"

Dad said, "Sleep time comes after bath time. Let's get you clean and cozy."

After dinner, Dad filled the tub with warm water. Muhammad splashed and played with his yellow duck. Dad washed his hair. Then Dad helped him dry off with the big soft towel.

Muhammad pulled his fire truck shirt from the chair. It was stiff and a little scratchy. He held it against his cheek. Then he looked at his pajamas on his bed. They were soft like his teddy bear. He touched the pajamas. He touched the shirt again. He put the shirt back on the chair.

"I will wear pajamas," said Muhammad. He put them on all by himself. The pajamas had little stars on them. He climbed into bed and hugged his teddy bear.

"The stars are for sleeping," said Muhammad. Dad smiled and turned off the light.

activity: celebrating a birthday with family and friends
knowledge_domain: celebrating a birthday with family and friends
fact: People say thank you when someone gives them a present.
story:
Maya turned four today. Her party was at the park. There was a big table with cake. Her friends came running up the grass.

Presents sat in a pile. Maya opened the first one. It was a little red truck from her friend Ben. She put it down fast. Then she grabbed the next box. Ben's face went sad and quiet.

Maya's mom knelt down beside her. "Do you like the truck?" she asked. Maya looked at Ben. "Should I say something to him?" she asked. Mom nodded. Maya ran back to Ben. "Thank you for the truck!" she said. Ben smiled big. "You can push it in the dirt," he said.

Then they sang the birthday song. Maya felt happy, not sick from worry anymore. Ben poured sand near the truck. Some sand did spill, but that was okay. Mom wiped it up. Maya pushed the red truck to Ben. "Your turn," she said. "Vroom!" said Ben.

activity: searching for a lost favorite toy
knowledge_domain: searching for a lost favorite toy
fact: Things can end up inside other things, like a toy tucked in a bag or coat pocket.
story:
Hazel went to the store with Dad. She held her bunny in the cart. But then the cart bumped over a bump. Bunny fell out! Hazel looked down. Bunny was not there.

Hazel looked by the apples. No bunny. She looked by the bread. No bunny. Dad walked slow so she could search. They passed the milk, so cold and white like a little lake in a jug. Still no bunny. Hazel wanted to cry.

Then Dad put a bag of carrots in the cart. The bag made a soft lump. Hazel peeked inside the bag. There was bunny! Bunny had fallen into the carrot bag. Hazel pulled bunny out and hugged her tight.

"Found you," Hazel said. Dad smiled. On the way home, Hazel put bunny inside her own coat pocket. She patted the pocket with her small hand. "Stay in there," she said. Bunny's ears poked out, soft and warm.

activity: simple safety concepts such as hot versus cold, staying close to caregivers and not touching dangerous objects
knowledge_domain: simple safety concepts such as hot versus cold, staying close to caregivers and not touching dangerous objects
fact: Stay where your grown-up can see you when you are out.
story:
Athena went to the backyard with Dad. Dad was cooking at the grill. "Stay close to me," said Dad. Athena stayed close to Dad.

Then Athena saw a butterfly. It flew to the far fence. Athena ran after it. She ran and ran. She could not see Dad anymore. The tall grass was all around her.

Athena stood still. She could not see Dad. Dad could not see her either. She felt a little scared. So she turned around. She walked back the way she came. She counted her steps. "One, two, three." Soon she saw Dad again. Dad waved his big hand.

"There you are," said Dad. He gave her a hug. The grill made a hot sizzle sound. Athena did not go near it. Dad said the grill was hot, and he held the long spoon himself. Athena watched from her safe spot on the step.

Then they heard a train far away. Choo, choo! Athena loved that sound. She sat with Dad on the step. He put a warm bun on her plate. It was not hot like the grill. It was just warm and neat. Athena took a bite. "Good," she said. Dad smiled and hugged her again.

activity: getting a vaccination shot at the doctor's office
knowledge_domain: getting a vaccination shot at the doctor's office
fact: After a shot, the nurse may put a small bandage over the spot.
story:
Ellie sat in a big chair at the doctor's office. Rain tapped on the window. Tap, tap, tap. "I don't want a pinchy arm," said Ellie. Mommy held her hand. "The nurse will be quick," said Mommy. The nurse came in with a small tray. "One, two, three, all done," said the nurse. One, two, three! Ellie felt one tiny poke, and then it was over. "You were so brave," said Mommy. "That was smart of you to hold still."

Then the nurse peeled open a little paper. It was a bandage with stars on it. She pressed it on Ellie's arm. "A star bandage," said the nurse. "Just for you." Ellie looked at it. The nurse had made the spot all better with one little sticker.

Afterward, Mommy took Ellie to the ice cream shop. Ellie got pink ice cream in a cup. It was cold and sweet. A fire truck went by outside, with a loud siren. Ellie held up her arm. "Look at my stars," she said to the lady at the counter. "One, two, three, four!" The lady clapped her hands. Ellie licked her ice cream and smiled.

activity: to recognise the letters of the alphabet and the sound each letter makes
knowledge_domain: to recognise the letters of the alphabet and the sound each letter makes
fact: Sun, sock and sand all start with the letter S and the 'sss' sound.
story:
Ayla sat in Grandma's cozy reading nook. It was cloudy outside, so they would play inside. Grandma held up a card with a big S. "This letter says sss," said Grandma. "Can you find things that say sss?"

Ayla looked around the room. She saw her sock on the rug. "Sss-sock!" she said. Grandma smiled and clapped.

Next Ayla ran to the window. The clouds were thick, but a little sun peeked through. "Sss-sun!" said Ayla. Grandma clapped again. Two things!

What else? Ayla tipped over her small shoe. No, that was a shoe. Then she saw her toy bucket. It was full of soft sand from the garden. She poked it with her finger. It felt warm and bumpy. "Sss-sand!" said Ayla. Grandma laughed and hugged her.

"You found three," said Grandma. Ayla held up the S card. "Sss," she said, and gave the card a big kiss.

activity: attending a religious or cultural celebration with family
knowledge_domain: attending a religious or cultural celebration with family
fact: People often wear special clothes to a celebration.
story:
Nathan woke up early. Today was the big festival. He looked at his little pile of clothes.

"What should I wear?" he asked Mama.

Mama laid out two shirts. One was old and soft. One was red and gold, with a shiny dragon on it. Nathan touched the dragon. It felt bumpy under his fingers.

He put on the red shirt. Then he took it off. Then he put it on again. Mama waited. She did not hurry him.

At the festival, the street smelled like sweet buns and flowers. Nathan saw Grandma in her long silk dress. He saw Uncle in his white coat with gold buttons. He saw cousins in bright, twirly skirts.

"You look like us," Grandma said with a big smile. "We all wear special clothes today."

Nathan looked down at his dragon shirt. His cousin had a dragon too. They held hands and walked up the little hill together.

Then the drums began. Boom, boom, boom. The dragon danced down the street, and its tail was wet from the morning rain. Nathan clapped and clapped.

"I picked this shirt," he told his cousin. "I picked it all by myself."

activity: starting the first day of school
knowledge_domain: starting the first day of school
fact: A school day has a time for eating a snack or lunch.
story:
Lea stood by the slide. It was her first day of school. Her tummy made a little growl. "I am hungry," she said. She wanted to grab her snack right now.

Her teacher, Miss Ana, knelt down. "First we play," said Miss Ana. "Then we all eat together. School has a snack time." Lea held her teacher's hand.

Lea pushed a toy truck. The truck rolled fast. She patted a fluffy toy animal. She went down the slide, not too high, just her size. Her tummy growled again.

Then Miss Ana rang a little bell. "Snack time!" she said. Lea sat at the small table with the other kids. She opened her bag. She took a bite of banana. It tasted so good. "We played, and now we eat," said Lea. Miss Ana smiled and gave her a cup of water.

activity: getting a first library card and borrowing a book
knowledge_domain: getting a first library card and borrowing a book
fact: Borrowed books have to be brought back to the library by a certain day, called the due date.
story:
Luna ran to the bookmobile. She picked a book about a red truck. The librarian gave her a little card. "Your first library card," she said. Luna smiled big.

"I want to keep the truck book forever," Luna said.

The librarian shook her head. "The book has to come back on its due day," she said. "Then another kid can read it too."

Luna held the book tight. "But I love it," she said.

"You can take it home now," the librarian said. "Bring it back, and then you can borrow a new one."

At home, Luna read the truck book three times. Mama helped her move it to a safe shelf. When the due day came, Luna put the book in her bag. "It is not mine," she said. "It goes back."

The bookmobile was not empty. A boy stood there, waiting. "I want the truck book," he said.

Luna gave it to the librarian. "Here," she said. "He can read it next."

"Thank you," said the boy. He sat down and opened the book.

Luna picked a new book about the moon. "This one is my gift for today," she said. The librarian laughed and stamped her card.

activity: to throw a beanbag into a hoop and catch a large ball with both hands
knowledge_domain: to throw a beanbag into a hoop and catch a large ball with both hands
fact: Standing closer to the hoop makes it easier to get the beanbag in.
story:
Jasmine stood far from the hoop. She threw the beanbag. It missed. She threw it again. It missed again.

"Big throw," said Dad. "Try again."

Jasmine took three little steps closer. One, two, three. She threw the beanbag. It went in! The hoop went swish.

Jasmine jumped up and down. Dad clapped his hands.

Then Dad held out a big red ball. "Catch it with both hands," he said. He rolled it slow. Jasmine held out her arms. One hand, two hands. The ball bumped her tummy and she grabbed it.

"Now throw it back," said Dad. Jasmine threw it high. Dad caught it and licked his ice cream. Their furry dog, Biscuit, barked at the ball.

"One more," said Jasmine. "One more hoop, one more catch, one more dog."

Biscuit wagged his tail.

activity: bringing home a first pet and learning to care for it
knowledge_domain: bringing home a first pet and learning to care for it
fact: A tag on a pet's collar tells people how to reach its family if the pet gets lost.
story:
Emile went to the vet with his mom. There was a small puppy in a cage. The puppy had soft brown ears. "We can take him home," Mom said. Emile gave the puppy a kiss on his head. The puppy wagged his tail.

The vet held up a little tag. It was shiny and round. Emile picked a blue one. The vet wrote their phone number on it. The tag went on the puppy's collar. It made a tiny tinkling sound.

At home, the puppy ran in the yard. Then he found a hole in the fence. Off he went. Emile felt scared. Soon a neighbor knocked on the door. She held the puppy. "I called the number on his tag," she said. Emile hugged the puppy tight. "I love you," he said. "And I love your tag." The puppy licked his cheek.

activity: making an art or craft project
knowledge_domain: making an art or craft project
fact: Washable markers wash off skin with soap and water.
story:
Clara sat at the big art table. She had a box of markers. She wanted to draw a butterfly. It would be pink and blue, with big wings.

Clara drew the wings. Then she drew more wings. The marker slipped. A blue line went right on her hand. Clara looked down. Was the blue line stuck on her skin forever?

"Look at my hand," Clara said. Her teacher, Mia, came over. Mia did not look worried at all. She smiled. "Let's go to the sink," said Mia. "What do you think will happen?"

Clara ran to the sink with Mia. Mia turned on the water. She helped Clara rub her hands with soap. Round and round went the bubbles. Clara watched the blue line. It began to fade. Then it was gone! Her hand was clean again.

"Where did the blue go?" Clara wondered. She looked at her hand. Then she looked at the markers. Maybe she should test it again. Clara drew one small dot on her finger. A cute little pink dot. She carried it back to show Mia. "This one can wash off too," Clara said. "I made it. And I can un-make it!" She wiggled her clean fingers at the butterfly on the table.

activity: hosting a grandparent who comes to stay for a week
knowledge_domain: hosting a grandparent who comes to stay for a week
fact: Hosts show a guest where things are, like the towels and the bathroom.
story:
Grandpa came to stay for a whole week. Maeva was so happy. She held his hand all the way to the park. The swings were far away, so they walked slowly.

"Want to swing?" asked Grandpa. "Yes!" said Maeva. Grandpa pushed her high. She could see the ducks on the pond. Then they went home for bread and milk. Grandpa had a bath. Maeva heard water splashing.

Then Grandpa yelled, "Oh dear! Where is a towel?" Maeva ran to the bathroom door. "I know!" she said. She opened the cupboard. It was low, just her size. She took out a soft blue towel and pushed it under the door. "Thank you, Maeva!" said Grandpa. "You are a good helper."

The next day Grandpa needed the soap. Maeva showed him the shelf. Then he needed a spoon, and she showed him the drawer. Grandpa laughed and laughed. At the park again, Maeva found a shiny red feather by the bench. She put it in Grandpa's pocket. "For you," she said. Grandpa grinned. "You show me everything, little host."
